trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out up, down, left or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.

Contradiction! Going left would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order), and that's the only legal move. So my guess (up from number 1) was wrong. Next I'll try down.
I can't rule out down or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.
Going left would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
I can't rule out right or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
Going right, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,5); going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up.
Cell (3,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Cell (1,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going left, the next 8 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,2). So the line goes down.
Number 5 is only reachable this way.
Cell (1,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going right would force the line onto number 8 before its turn. So the line goes down.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Going right would cut off the left side (4 cells); going down would leave number 8 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up.
Going right would strand number 8: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right would leave number 10 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
Going down would cut off the bottom-left corner (6 cells). So the line goes left.
Going down would cut off the bottom-left corner (4 cells). So the line goes left.
Cell (6,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (7,7) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going up would cut off the bottom-right corner (4 cells). So the line goes left.
Going up would leave both cell (5,5) and cell (5,7) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
